repositories.name: nk-missile-tests
repositories.description: An interactive visualization of flight tests of all missiles launched by North Korea from 1984 to 2026

paragraphs: An interactive visualization of flight tests of all missiles launched by North Korea from 1984 to 2026. The real-time positions of North Korea's satellites are also visualized on the globe.

The data for this visualization are sourced from the CNS North Korea Missile Test Database, which is the first database to record flight tests of all missiles launched by North Korea capable of delivering a payload of at least 500 kilograms (1102.31 pounds) a distance of at least 300 kilometers (186.4 miles). The database captures advancements in North Korea's missile program by documenting all such tests since the first one occurred in April 1984, and will be routinely updated as events warrant.

The CNS North Korea Missile Test Database doesn't include the exact landing locations, so we have added bearing information from other sources such as Japan Ministry of Defense, and landing locations are calculated based on locations of launching facilities and distances travelled.

whatItDoes.text: An interactive visualization of flight tests of all missiles launched by North Korea from 1984 to 2026. The real-time positions of North Korea's satellites are also visualized on the globe.

paragraphs: Terminuler is a full-stack appointment booking system. Customers pick a weekday, choose a free one-hour slot, enter their contact details and get a confirmation email. Loading, error and success states are shown for every step. Validation errors show the API's message. A rate-limited booking (429) asks the customer to wait. Other errors show a generic message.
Accessible, keyboard-friendly controls (native inputs, labelled fields, aria-pressed slots, focus management) and a responsive layout.

paragraphs: Catch breaking changes in AI vendor APIs before your code does.

ModelPulse watches 15 public AI vendor changelog pages daily, normalizes them into a single schema, and alerts you on Slack/Discord the moment a breaking change ships. When a vendor redesigns their page, the pipeline auto-heals itself — no code change, no redeployment. Built for the Scrape-Verse Hackathon with Bright Data Scraper Studio.
Because subscribing isn't the problem — normalizing, scoring, and acting is. The 15-second answer:
features: Half these vendors have no feed at all. Mistral, Cohere, Groq, Together, Fireworks, Replicate publish changelogs as plain HTML pages. There is nothing to subscribe to.

Feeds only tell you what's new — never what was edited. Vendors silently rewrite published entries. ModelPulse diffs every field on every scrape and flags silent edits (the ↻ EDITED badge).
Per vendor: /feed/openai, /feed/anthropic, … (any vendor slug)
CORS is enabled — call it from anywhere.

repositories.name: learn-openhands-harness
repositories.description: A hands-on course in harness engineering with OpenHands: the system around the model (routing, tools, memory, safety, critics, workflow).

paragraphs: Website: rajshah4.github.io/learn-openhands-harness

Every coding agent ships two things: a model that reasons and a harness that does everything else. The harness decides what the model sees, which tools it can call, what it remembers across turns, when it stops, and whether it runs in a sandbox or on your bare machine. This translates into implications for performance, reliability, and latency.

This tutorial gives you a working harness you can open, run, and change. You'll use two open-source projects, Agent Server (the HTTP API that owns the workspace, conversation state, and tool dispatch) and Agent Canvas (the operator UI), as a microscope. You'll give the agent real tasks, read the trace of what happened, and then change one lever at a time to see the behavior shift.
features: Clean client/server split. The agent server is a stateless-ish HTTP API; the canvas is a thin client. The harness boundary is literally an OpenAPI spec. You can replace either side without rewriting the other.
Three deployment shapes from one codebase. Local process, Docker sandbox, hosted API, all by swapping a Workspace class. That makes the cost of where work runs visible.

The trace is a first-class object. The chronological record of messages, tool calls, results, compaction, and confirmations is right there in the canvas. You don't have to grep logs to see what the harness is doing.

whatItDoes.text: Website: rajshah4.github.io/learn-openhands-harness

repositories.description: HTMX for ASP.NET Core: typed HX-* headers, fluent responses, Tag Helpers, and antiforgery. Supports HTMX 1.9, 2, and 4.

paragraphs: HtmxToolkit helps you build HTMX applications with ASP.NET Core.

HTMX and the server talk through HX- headers. Requests carry details such as the target element and the current URL, and your response can tell HTMX where to put the HTML, whether to change the URL, or which events to raise. HtmxToolkit lets you do all of this from C# and Razor, without header strings or hand-written JSON:
HtmxToolkit runs on .NET 6 or later and supports HTMX 1.9.x, 2.x, and 4.x. HTMX 2.x is the default.
features: Find out whether HTMX expects a fragment or a full page, and read its headers as typed properties.
Tell HTMX what to do next with a fluent API: retarget, reswap, redirect, push a URL, or trigger an event.
Send HTMX requests to dedicated MVC actions with [HtmxRequest].
Build hx-get and hx-post URLs from controllers, actions, and Razor Pages, just like the asp- Tag Helpers do.
Configure HTMX once in Program.cs and send antiforgery tokens with HTMX requests automatically.

whatItDoes.text: HtmxToolkit helps you build HTMX applications with ASP.NET Core.

paragraphs: Plug-and-play object tracking in Python (multi-object) for any detection model.

trackers is an object tracking library for Python. supervision.Detections native. Plugs directly into the supervision ecosystem. Pass detections in, get tracked detections back — zero glue code.

paragraphs: This project measures what happens to London's cycle-hire demand when the wider transport network is disrupted. Transport for London has published cycle-hire journeys since 2012, as CSV files in a public S3 bucket. An inventory of that bucket counted roughly 189M trips across 482 files — a dated snapshot taken once, not a claim about what the bucket holds today. The backfill actually built here covers 41.4M journeys in 148 retained files from 2022 to May 2026, spanning five different column layouts, because TfL renamed, dropped and reordered columns between eras.

paragraphs: Vouch is an evidence-first brand-governance reviewer. paragraphs: Production-grade document intelligence engineered with hybrid vector + BM25 retrieval, multi-key failover LLM pipeline, and strict source citations — accuracy-first, zero hallucination.

Docly is engineered for source-grounded document intelligence. Every answer is deterministically tied to exact document chunks and page citations ([Source 1, Page 14]). If retrieved context is insufficient or unverified, Docly will explicitly decline to speculate rather than hallucinate.

Docly is a full-stack, multi-tenant AI Document Knowledge Base SaaS designed for modern engineering, legal, research, and executive teams. Rather than treating document Q&A as a generic chatbot wrapper, Docly treats document intelligence as a strict, verifiable retrieval problem.
features: Zero Hallucination Tolerance: Answers are synthesized exclusively from verified document context. If information is not in the source materials, Docly explicitly declares it.
Sub-Second Streaming: Powered by a 3-Key Groq failover rotation delivering up to 250 tokens/second, paired with Google Gemini 1.5 fallback for extended-context tasks.
Client-Side Document Parsing & OCR: In-browser PDF font decoding (ToUnicode CMaps) and Tesseract OCR ensure zero server bottlenecks and airtight client data privacy.
Multi-Tenant Collaboration: Enterprise-ready team invitations, dynamic RBAC (Owner, Editor, Viewer), and instant notification centers.

Zero Cascading Failures: If Groq encounters rate limiting or temporary latency spikes, the system automatically rotates across redundant API keys or cascades to Gemini Flash without user interruption.

whatItDoes.text: Production-grade document intelligence engineered with hybrid vector + BM25 retrieval, multi-key failover LLM pipeline, and strict source citations — accuracy-first, zero hallucination.

paragraphs: Production grade AI backend platform built around memory-efficient ingestion, async HTTP, and eventually hybrid RAG retrieval with LangGraph agents.

Core idea: most AI pipelines fail at scale not because of the model, but because of poor infrastructure - loading files eagerly into memory, firing unbounded concurrent requests, or writing everything to disk at once. This project builds the infrastructure layer that handles all of that correctly.

Built incrementally over 12 phases, roughly one per week. Each lab isolates one concept, breaks it, measures it, fixes it, then integrates it into the platform. Code in core/ is production-ready - scripts in scripts/ show how it was built and tested.

whatItDoes.text: Production grade AI backend platform built around memory-efficient ingestion, async HTTP, and eventually hybrid RAG retrieval with LangGraph agents.

paragraphs: A browser-ready efficient scrolling container based on UITableView.
React Infinite 0.7.1 only supports React 0.14 and above. Please pin your package to 0.6.0 for React 0.13 support.

When a long list of DOM elements are placed in a scrollable container, all of them are kept in the DOM even when they are out the user's view. This is highly inefficient, especially in cases when scrolling lists can be tens or hundreds of thousands of items long. React Infinite solves this by rendering only DOM nodes that the user is able to see or might soon see. Other DOM nodes are clustered and rendered as a single blank node.

Ein MLP (Stück 2) behandelt jedes Beispiel unabhängig. Ein RNN (Elman 1990) trägt einen Zustand über eine Sequenz – jeder Zeitschritt aktualisiert denselben Zustand mit denselben (geteilten) Gewichten. Hier zum ersten Mal: Vehikel C, eine Signal-in-Rauschen-Sequenz der Länge $T$, die auch die nächsten beiden Stücke (LSTM, Attention/Transformer) tragen wird.

Ergebnis in Kürze: Ein Bit Information über eine Sequenz zu tragen gelingt bei kurzen Sequenzen fast immer (100 % Erfolgsquote bei $T\le10$), wird aber mit wachsendem $T$ zunehmend eine Frage des Zufalls (nur noch 33–40 % bei $T\ge80$) – nicht weil das RNN es nicht könnte, sondern weil der Gradient, der das lernen soll, unterwegs praktisch verschwindet: die Gradientennorm am ERSTEN Zeitschritt fällt von $\approx1{,}2$ bei $T=2$ auf $6{,}7\cdot10^{-11}$ bei $T=150$ (über 10 Zehnerpotenzen), während sie am LETZTEN Zeitschritt konstant bei $\approx1$ bleibt.

repositories.name: wellenfreigabe-demo
repositories.description: Kommissionierwellen mit Fristen und Gangblockaden: Wie viel kostet Blockieren, und wann lohnt Konfliktvermeidung? (Streamlit-Demo, CP-SAT-Referenz)

paragraphs: Interaktive Fall-Demo (Lager-Linie): Kommissionierer arbeiten vorgebildete Batches mit Versandfristen ab und laufen dabei durch schmale Gänge, in denen sie sich nicht überholen können – jeder Gang ist eine Einzelressource mit FIFO-Warteschlange am Eingang. Die Demo beantwortet: Wie viel kostet das Blockieren, wie viel vom Vorteil einer Fristenregel bleibt dann übrig – und wann lohnt es sich, Gangkonflikte gezielt zu vermeiden, obwohl man dafür dringende Batches zurückstellt?

Teil des Portfolios für die Website „Sebastian Hanisch – Operations Research und Machine Learning“. Erweiterung der Batching-Demo (orderbatch-demo, „baut aus“): sie hebt zwei stillschweigende Annahmen dort auf – dass Batches ohne Fristen bearbeitet werden und dass gleichzeitig arbeitende Kommissionierer sich nicht behindern (vermerkt in deren „Bewusst nicht enthalten“ und „Anpassungsideen“). Regeln im Vergleich: FIFO, EDD (frühester Fristbatch zuerst), EDD mit Konflikt-Fenster w (Regler 1 bis 8, w = 1 ist EDD) und, nur für Kleininstanzen, das exakte Optimum (CP-SAT) als Maßstab.

repositories.description: SyncScribe: real-time collaborative editor with Yjs, a self-hosted Hocuspocus server, GitHub sign-in, server-enforced owner/editor/viewer roles and version history. Live demo runs fully in your browser.

paragraphs: A real-time collaborative document editor with role-based sharing, version history and a self-hosted Yjs sync server.
Live demo: shashank11yadav.github.io/SyncScribe. This is the in-browser demo: it runs entirely in your browser and syncs between your own tabs, with no server behind it.
Two tabs of the GitHub Pages build editing the same document. Captured from the production build with apps/demo/e2e/readme-media.spec.ts.
features: Live co-editing. Yjs merges concurrent edits character by character. Remote cursors show each person's name, and a presence list shows who is in the document.
Owner, editor and viewer roles. Checked on every server action and route handler, and again by the sync server, which gives viewers a read-only socket.
Sharing by email. Works the same whether or not the address has an account yet, so the share dialog cannot be used to find out who has signed up.
Live revocation. Removing someone or lowering their role closes their socket within a second; their next connection gets the new permissions.
Version history. Snapshots are taken while people write. Any version can be previewed and restored, and a restore never destroys the text it replaces.

whatItDoes.text: A real-time collaborative document editor with role-based sharing, version history and a self-hosted Yjs sync server.

repositories.name: QuDock
repositories.description: Explore this public GitHub project.

paragraphs: QuDock tests whether a quantum kernel can find BACE-1 inhibitors (a key Alzheimer's drug target) better than classical machine learning when data is scarce and hardware is noisy. Molecules from the MoleculeNet BACE dataset (1,513) are turned into fingerprints, compressed to one angle per qubit and loaded into a ZZ feature map. A quantum kernel SVM is compared with SVM-RBF, Random Forest and Logistic Regression on identical features, using a scaffold split, 25 to 1,210 training molecules, 2 to 10 qubits and multiple seeds. The quantum model matches the RBF SVM (best ROC-AUC 0.719 at 8 qubits)…

repositories.name: Pixelbolt
repositories.description: Agent-first pixel art and animation toolkit. JSON recipes to PNG, APNG and sprite atlases via CLI, MCP server and local studio. Zero dependencies. MIT.

paragraphs: Pixel art and sprite animation that your AI agent can make, check and fix. Pixelbolt turns an editable JSON recipe into sprites, tiles, icons, effects and short animations, and exports them as PNG sprite sheets, texture atlases, animated PNGs, GIFs and frames for a video editor. Agents drive it through a local MCP server or the command line; you can open, play and edit the same recipe in a local browser studio.
Try it in your browser: render, export and share recipes with nothing installed.

Fire, smoke, steam, explosions, magic, water, honey and slime come from a real fluid simulation that runs on your own CPU in well under a second and bakes every frame into palette pixels you can edit, with seamless loops (fluid effects).
features: Who it's for: game developers, game-jam teams and web or video makers who want an agent such as Claude, Codex or Cursor to draw and revise their pixel art, and people building agents that need exact, repeatable images.

Use it when you want small 2D game assets that stay editable as text: the agent reads every pixel back, fixes one pixel or one frame without redrawing the rest, and the same recipe renders the same image every time.

Don't use it for painted, photographic or large images (a frame is at most 256 × 256 pixels, and a project at most 256 frames and 4,194,304 pixels in all), generating art with an image model, or editing GIFs and…

C ++ classes by default do not have the required meta-object information for serializing class fields, but Qt is equipped with its own highly efficient meta-object system. An important feature of the QSerializer is the ability to specify serializable fields of the class without having to serialize the entire class. QSerilaizer generate code and declare QPROPERTY for every declared member of class. This is convenient because you do not need to create separate structures or classes…

repositories.name: locus
repositories.description: Local-first vault for linked notes, a spatial canvas, a reactive notebook, and cited answers on the device.

paragraphs: A local vault for linked notes. The text stays in the browser.

Locus is a writing desk for one device. You write a note, type / for a block and @ for another note, and the same notes can sit on a canvas, feed a small reactive notebook, or answer a question in Atlas with the passage they came from.
There is no account. The vault is stored in the browser. Export is a markdown file you download on purpose.
features: Notes. The visual editor is the default. Type / for a block (figure, sticker, photo, camera, video, map, note link, heading, list, checklist, quote, divider, code) or tap +. Type @ to link a note by name. A reading view…
Photos and video. Gallery, in-app camera, a short clip, drag-and-drop and paste. Images are resized on the device and kept in IndexedDB. Nothing is uploaded.

Private notes. Trancar nota encrypts the note on the device (PBKDF2 and AES-GCM). The list shows a padlock and the title, or hides the title. A forgotten password cannot be recovered. Unlock lasts for the session, then…
Canvas. Each card is a whole note. Moving it does not copy the text. Lines follow the links between notes. A locked note does not preview its text.
Notebook. A small interpreter (mean, std, chart, and the rest) runs cells by dependency, not by screen order.

whatItDoes.text: A local vault for linked notes. The text stays in the browser.

repositories.name: sql.js
repositories.description: A javascript library to run SQLite on the web.

paragraphs: sql.js is a javascript SQL database. It allows you to create a relational database and query it entirely in the browser. You can try it in this online demo. It uses a virtual database file stored in memory, and thus doesn't persist the changes made to the database. However, it allows you to import any existing sqlite file, and to export the created database as a JavaScript typed array.
sql.js uses emscripten to compile SQLite to WebAssembly. It includes contributed math and string extension functions.

sql.js can be used like any traditional JavaScript library. If you are building a native application in JavaScript (using Electron for instance), or are working in node.js, you will likely prefer to use a native binding of SQLite to JavaScript. A native binding will not only be faster because it will run native code, but it will also be able to work on database files directly instead of having to load the entire database in memory, avoiding out of memory errors and further improving performances.

repositories.name: swap_two_words_singly_linked_list
repositories.description: Explore this public GitHub project.

paragraphs: Recently I've been giving interviews as my last contract got completed. In one of the interviews, I was asked to write a data structure for a string using a singly linked list. The constraint was that the string would have exactly two words separated by a space. The task was to swap the position of the two words in an efficient way.
I started thinking and at the high level, it looked like a simple task where I had to just restructure the list by reassigning some of the pointers.

After some deliberation, I started writing the code to accomplish the task. Working with linked lists is something that we programmers rarely do in the real world. So, It took me a while to complete even half of the task (i.e., to move the second word to the beginning) and due to time constraints I couldn't complete the task during the interview. But I endured post the call and completed the task.

repositories.name: albedo
repositories.description: Security-centric, developer-friendly, easy-to-use delegated signer and keystore for Stellar Network

paragraphs: Albedo provides a safe and reliable way to use Stellar accounts without trusting anyone with a secret key.

It works like a bridge for other applications that allows them to ask permissions to sign a transaction or verify identity on user's behalf, so the same account can be used across the whole universe of Stellar applications. Sensitive data is encrypted and safely stored in the browser – no one has access to user's secret key.

From the developer's perspective, it takes only a few lines of code to turn any website into a production-ready Stellar wallet. Transactions building, signing, validation, errors handling – we have everything covered. There is no need to implement a keystore, build a dozen interfaces for transaction processing, and worry about security. In fact, things like payment request can be implemented without any coding at all, therefore allowing instant "stellarization" of any marketplace or even simple Wordpress site by simply copy-pasting code produced by the payment request generator.

Intent library – a lightweight browser wrapper for Albedo API
Secure key management – secret keys never exposed to third-party services.
Secure transaction signing – browser sandbox guarantees isolated transactions
signing environment.

paragraphs: FUNDING REQUIRED please contact me to support this work

Canvas is a common vector drawing target that can output SVG, PDF, EPS, raster images (PNG, JPG, GIF, ...), HTML Canvas through WASM, OpenGL, and Gio. It has a wide range of path manipulation functionality such as flattening, stroking and dashing implemented. Additionally, it has a text formatter and embeds and subsets fonts (TTF, OTF, WOFF, WOFF2, or EOT) or converts them to outlines. It can be considered a Cairo or node-canvas alternative in Go. See the example below in Figure 1 for an overview of the functionality.

Figure 1: top-left you can see text being fitted into a box, justified using Donald Knuth's linea breaking algorithm to stretch the spaces between words to fill the whole width. You can observe a variety of styles and text decorations applied, as well as support for LTR/RTL mixing and complex scripts. In the bottom-right the word "stroke" is being stroked and drawn as a path. Top-right we see a LaTeX formula that has been converted to a path. Left of that we see an ellipse showcasing precise dashing, notably the length of e.g. the short dash is equal wherever it is on the curve. Note that the…
features: Path segment types: MoveTo, LineTo, QuadTo, CubeTo, ArcTo, Close (see Paths)
Precise path flattening, stroking, and dashing for all segment types (see papers below)
Smooth spline generation through points for open and closed paths
LaTeX to path conversion (native Go and CGO implementations available)
sRGB compliance (use SRGBColorSpace, only available for rasterizer)

repositories.name: tasty
repositories.description: A deterministic styling engine for stateful component systems.

paragraphs: Tasty is a styling engine for teams that build component libraries. You describe hover, disabled, variants, themes, and breakpoints as state maps, in a CSS-like language built from your design system's own tokens and conventions. Tasty compiles each map into selectors that never match at the same time, so the result never depends on specificity or source order.

Later keys have higher priority. If this button is both hovered and disabled, [disabled] wins and the hover rule does not apply. That decision is compiled into the selectors themselves, so you can add states, variants, themes, and overrides without reopening selector logic by hand.
features: Ready to try it? Follow Getting Started.
Building a component library? See Methodology and Building a Design System.

States that can't conflict — Every state map compiles into mutually exclusive selectors, and the last matching key wins by construction. Adding a state, variant, or override never means re-deriving selector…

Your design system's language — Define color tokens, units, state aliases like @mobile and @dark, typography presets, and recipes once with configure(). Components then read like the spec: padding: '2x', fill:…

Typed component APIs — Decide exactly what consumers can change. styleProps, modProps, tokenProps, variants, and sub-elements become typed React props and components with full autocomplete. Component API →

Describe a sound and write lyrics — or give it a one-line idea — and it plans the song with its language model and renders it with vocals on your own graphics card. repositories.name: a2a-trust-playground
repositories.description: Explore this public GitHub project.

paragraphs: A browser implementation of draft-tonyai-a2a-trust-03 — an IETF Internet-Draft on agent-to-agent trust: identity carried in X.509, spawn authorization attested by the CA, scope delegation, dual-signed policy governance, cross-organizational grants, revocation and audit integrity.

Mint a Registry and two agents, delegate a narrower identity to the child, then try to widen it and watch the chain refuse — citing the clause of the draft that refused it. No install, no account, no API key, and nothing transmitted: every key is generated in your tab by Web Crypto and is gone when you refresh.

The draft has a reference implementation (ietf-a2a-trust-poc) and an adversarial one that attacks its own implementation (hack-my-own-code). Both need Docker, and one needs an API key. So the barrier to being the draft's next implementer was "read the spec and build a CA from scratch."

paragraphs: Inspired by [twitter.com]'s autocomplete search functionality, typeahead.js is a flexible JavaScript library that provides a strong foundation for building robust typeaheads.

paragraphs: Background and design notes (Japanese): Jevのキラーアプリ、「意味で探す grep」を作った on Zenn.

Renamed from semgrep (0.5.0). Two reasons. The name collided with the static-analysis tool Semgrep, a trademark. And the tool was never meant for Jev alone: it targets System 1 models in general, and I'd like it to work with any models TypeSafe AI may release after Jev under other names :). So from 0.5.0 this is sys1grep (System 1 + grep): npm package @uehaj/sys1grep (was @uehaj/semgrep), commands sys1grep / git sys1grep, environment SYS1GREP, config /.config/sys1grep/.env. The old SEMGREP names and /.config/semgrep/.env still work for one minor release, each use printing a deprecation line;…

A grep that finds lines by what they mean, not by regular expressions. Matching is done by Jev, the System One model from TypeSafe AI. Jev does not generate text. It answers typed questions with probabilities, so for every line sys1grep asks "does this line match the meaning network failure?", gets a probability back, and applies a threshold.
features: Zero dependencies. Node.js 20.16+ and fetch, nothing else.
Fast. 30 lines go into one request, requests run 8 at a time (1 for a local URL). A 210-line file finishes in under a second.
Meanings combine with AND / OR / NOT.
Language-agnostic. The meaning and the text can each be in any language. A Japanese meaning finds French, Russian, Chinese and Korean lines alike. No translation step, same speed, same cost.

repositories.name: berrry-wine
repositories.description: Run real Windows 98 apps and games in your browser. An x86 emulator and Win32 layer written directly in WebAssembly Text, no OS image, no source ports.

paragraphs: Try it now → wine-assembly.berrry.app · Apps you can run · The story of how it was built · How it works: articles, design docs & reverse-engineering notes

Wine-Assembly is a Windows 98 emulator for the browser that runs the original, unmodified .exe files. There is no operating-system image to boot and no source port to maintain: an x86 interpreter and a reimplementation of the Win32 API are written directly in WebAssembly Text (WAT), and the program's own machine code runs on them. Pinball, SkiFree, Solitaire, Minesweeper, Notepad, Paint, Winamp, DirectX games and 16-bit Windows 3.1 programs all launch in a tab, on desktop and on a phone.

Large parts of the reverse engineering, implementation, testing, and documentation were developed in collaboration with Claude Code and Codex. PROJECTSTORY.md reconstructs that history from Git and the agent sessions that built it.

repositories.name: osu-browser
repositories.description: osu! stable in a browser tab: play and map beatmaps, with a stable-style editor

paragraphs: The app is called osu!browser. The repository, npm package, Docker image and URLs drop the ! (osu-browser), because that's easier for folder names and links.

osu!browser puts osu! (stable) in a browser tab: play your maps and map them, on any laptop. Drop an mp3 to start a new map, or open an .osz / beatmap folder to keep editing or to play it. When you're done, export the .osz (or a single .osu) and open it in osu!. Uploading to the osu! website isn't supported; use the real client for that.

It follows stable's flow: the main menu (the cookie: Play, Edit, Options, Exit), then song select in play or edit mode, then the game or the editor; Esc or "back" takes you back each time. Playing is mostly there to test your maps: scores stay in the browser, in song select's local ranking. Like stable, nothing autosaves in the editor: Ctrl+S saves the set in the browser (IndexedDB), and leaving with unsaved changes asks first. If you connect your Google Drive (optional), saving also syncs your maps to an "osu-browser" folder in it, so they're there when you open the app on another computer.…
features: Main menu & play mode

[x] Stable's main menu: the cookie pulsing on the beat (brighter in kiai) with a visualiser ring, Play / Edit / Options / Exit sliding out (P, E, O, D for osu!direct), user panel with local plays and accuracy, "You have…

[x] Play-mode song select: Enter plays, Ctrl+Enter plays with Autoplay, F1 mod selection, local ranking (click a score for its ranking screen, right-click to delete it), the info panel's stats and star rating with the…

[x] Mod selection like stable's: Difficulty Reduction (EZ NF HT), Difficulty Increase (HR SD/PF DT/NC HD FL), Special (RX AP SO AU/CN V2), score multiplier, Q W E / A S D F G / Z X C V B keys, 1 reset, 2 close; icons…

[x] osu!standard gameplay as stable judges it: 300/100/50 windows from OD, notelock (and the early-click miss), sliders scored on head, ticks, repeats and tail (36 ms leniency, follow circle 2.4× once tracking),…

repositories.name: wickra-impact
repositories.description: The backtester that knows you would have moved the market: agent-based fills on the real historical L2 order book.

paragraphs: The backtester that knows you would have moved the market — agent-based fills on the real historical L2 order book, so slippage is measured, not guessed.

Every ordinary backtest lies: it fills your order at the close, or at a fixed slippage estimate, as if your size were invisible. Wickra Impact does not. It walks your order through the actual recorded L2 order book — eating liquidity level by level — so the fill price is what the market would really have given you, impact included.

Impact is one library, wickra-impact-core: it inherits the wickra-backtest engine 1:1 (its StrategySpec, RunRequest and BacktestReport) and replaces only the fill stage with an order-book-walk fill engine. It is usable in Rust, Python, Node.js, WASM, C, C++, C#, Go, Java and R over a JSON-over-C-ABI boundary (commandjson), plus a reference CLI.

whatItDoes.text: The backtester that knows you would have moved the market — agent-based fills on the real historical L2 order book, so slippage is measured, not guessed.

paragraphs: exprcodegen本质是DSL，领域特定语⾔(Domain Specific Language)。但它没有定义新的语法
就算在量化领域，初级研究员局限于时序指标，仅用polarsta即可，中高级研究员使用截面指标，推荐用exprcodegen

features: polarsta已经能很方便的写出特征计算表达式，但遇到混用时序与截面的表达式，利用exprcodegen能自动分组大大节省工作
exprcodegen利用了Common Subexpression Elimination公共子表达式消除，大量减少重复计算，提高效率

repositories.name: han
repositories.description: A compiled programming language with Korean keywords, written in Rust

paragraphs: A general-purpose compiled language with Korean keywords, types, built-ins, and standard library — written in Rust

Han is a statically-typed, compiled programming language where keywords, type names, 50+ built-in functions, and standard library methods are written in Korean — with all error messages in Korean too. Arithmetic, comparison, and assignment operators follow C/Rust conventions. It compiles to native binaries through LLVM IR and also ships with a tree-walking interpreter for instant execution. The compiler toolchain is written entirely in Rust.
features: Korean keywords — 함수, 만약, 이면, 반복, 변수, 상수, 반환, 구조, 시도, 처리, 맞춤
Korean word order — 만약 조건 이면 { }, 조건 동안 { } (SOV) and 동안 조건 { } (SVO)
Korean logical operators — 그리고 (and), 또는 (or)
Hangul identifiers — name your variables, functions, fields in Korean
Compiled & interpreted — hgl build (LLVM IR → clang → binary) or hgl interpret for instant runs

whatItDoes.text: A general-purpose compiled language with Korean keywords, types, built-ins, and standard library — written in Rust

repositories.name: random-geographic-coordinates-generator
repositories.description: Generate reproducible random geographic coordinates worldwide, on land, by country, around a point, inside a bounding box, or within a custom polygon.

paragraphs: Random Geographic Coordinates Generator is a lightweight, browser-based tool for creating random latitude and longitude data for mapping, software testing, GIS experiments, education, logistics research, and location-based product development. The project is designed to work as a fast static website that can be hosted on GitHub Pages without a backend, database, account system, or paid API.

The generator supports several geographic constraints instead of producing only unrestricted global coordinates. Users can create points across the entire Earth, restrict results to land, select a country, generate points around a known center, define a bounding box, or draw a custom polygon directly on the map. The generated dataset can be previewed, copied, and exported immediately.

The interface is responsive and works on desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices. It is also configured as a Progressive Web App, so the application can be installed and reopened using cached local resources. The Service Worker follows a network-first strategy: each visit requests the latest files from the server first and falls back to the cache when the network request fails.

whatItDoes.text: Random Geographic Coordinates Generator is a lightweight, browser-based tool for creating random latitude and longitude data for mapping, software testing, GIS experiments, education, logistics research, and location-based product development. The project is designed to work as a fast static website that can be hosted on GitHub Pages without a backend, database, account system, or paid API.

repositories.name: saxl
repositories.description: SAXL: Software Architecture eXpression Language

paragraphs: saxl (Software Architecture eXpression Language) is a small text language for describing a software system once and generating every architecture view from that one description: context, containers, runtime scenarios, data, deployment, and a 3D "tower" that stacks them all. It can describe a library the same way.

Because every view comes from the same model, the views can't contradict each other. And because the model is structured, it can be checked: the validator works like a type checker for the architecture, catching scenarios that use connections nobody declared, services with nowhere to run, data with no source of truth, and single points of failure.

repositories.name: vocarb
repositories.description: A vocabulary flashcard app for Arabic and Chinese vocab for my class

paragraphs: Minimalist Arabic–Chinese vocabulary flashcards.

A single-page flashcard app for studying Arabic vocabulary with Chinese and English translations. Built for a small class: anyone can study and takequizzes, while the word bank is managed by the owner through a hidden admin mode. Vocabulary lives in Supabase (PostgreSQL), English meanings are fetched through a free keyless translation API via a Vercel serverless function, and new words are added inside the app.
features: Bulk import — paste a weekly word list (Chinese + Arabic per line); the parser handles numbered and bulleted WhatsApp-style lists, auto-swaps reversed sides, strips cross-script contamination (e.g. a stray Chinese…
Sets — organize words into sets (Week 12, Week 13, …) or review everything
Both directions — CN → AR or AR → CN; pinyin shown above Chinese, full harakat on the Arabic
Keyboard-first — Space to flip, arrow keys to navigate
Shuffle for randomized review

whatItDoes.text: Minimalist Arabic–Chinese vocabulary flashcards.

repositories.name: shotlate
repositories.description: 小而精的 macOS 截图工具：标注、贴图、长截图、文字识别、原位翻译

paragraphs: 小而精的 macOS 截图工具：快捷键截图、标注、贴图、长截图。另外加了原位翻译：识别截图里的外文，翻译后直接画回原文的位置。默认用免费翻译，装完就能用；想要更好的效果，可以换成自己的大模型。
一次完整的截图：悬停选中窗口，框选，画框、箭头和序号，最后按 X 识别文字。画面由 Shotlate 的截图界面直接渲染。
features: 文字识别使用系统自带的 Vision 框架，在本机完成。
翻译默认使用免费的腾讯交互翻译，不需要配置；也可以改用 OpenAI 兼容的大模型（如 DeepSeek 的 deepseek-flash）。只发送识别出的文字，截图本身不上传。
纯 Swift 编写，唯一的第三方依赖是负责自动更新的 Sparkle。要求 macOS 14 或更高版本。
小：安装包约 3.5 MB（Apple 芯片和 Intel 通用），常驻菜单栏时内存占用约 50 MB。
